concepts.def: Christian place of worship and community.
Largest denomination; led by the Pope in Rome.
Eastern Christian tradition centred on patriarchs.

walkthroughs.body_html: Christianity has three main branches. Catholics (largest) are led by the Pope in Rome. Orthodox Christians follow ancient Eastern traditions and patriarchs. Protestants split from Catholicism in the 1500s and include Anglicans, Methodists, Baptists and many more.

A church typically has an altar (for communion), pews or chairs (for worshippers), a cross, a pulpit (for sermons), a font (for baptism), and often stained glass windows. Different denominations decorate their churches differently.

Most Christians celebrate special rituals called sacraments, especially baptism (welcoming someone into the faith with water) and Holy Communion / Eucharist (sharing bread and wine in memory of Jesus's Last Supper).
